get.summary: List the vendor integration catalog, license/feature-flag filtered.
get.description:
Lists the static vendor integration catalog (271 configs), served from the git-authored
corpus (`catalog/data/*.yaml`) and tenant-filtered exactly like the SDK's own
`Integrations().get_config()` did (verified bug-for-bug -- see
`services.catalog.filtering`'s module docstring): a KIND within a vendor that requires a
license/feature-flag the tenant lacks is omitted from that vendor's `kinds`, but the
vendor-level `required_licenses` check (e.g. AI Governance) never omits the whole vendor --
that gate is dead code in the underlying SDK on the live serving path, and this endpoint
intentionally reproduces that, not a stricter (but non-equivalent) reading of it. Optionally
filtered to a single integration type via the `type` query param (e.g. `VENDOR` or
`INTEGRATION_TYPE_VENDOR`).

get.description: Paginated list of a tenant's business nodes, with a vendor-doc fallback for BUSINESS_ENTITY nodes' description/business-models. Mirrors enterprise-api GET /v1/internal/business-nodes.

Lists every connection configured for a vendor, from the tenant's `vendors` document
(`vendors.integrations`). Each entry is the raw connection sub-doc (SDK/mgr field
names preserved) plus its `id`.

post.summary: Create a new connection for a vendor.
post.description:
Creates a new connection for a vendor. Allocates the next per-vendor connection id
(mirrors mgr's monotonic `vendor_connection_next_id` counter) and seeds the
`vendors.integrations.<id>` sub-doc with `auth: {type: null, status: AUTH_STATUS_NOT_CONNECTED}`.

When the vendor's `status` is `Inactive`, an existing never-configured connection with the
same `connection_name`/`integrationType` is reused (its id is returned) instead of creating a
duplicate. Otherwise the new connection is auto-associated with the tenant's own business
entity (`business_node_ids`) if one exists, and auto-selects `kinds` the vendor only supports
one of, plus `INTEGRATION_KIND_PROPERTY_INSPECTION` and the always-enabled kinds
(`INTEGRATION_KIND_ASSETS_DISCOVERY`, `INTEGRATION_KIND_AI_DISCOVERY`) when the vendor supports
them (mirrors mgr's `create_connection`).

Returns 201 with the created connection resource (the sub-doc as stored, including `id`) and
a `Location` header pointing at `GET .../connections/v1/{vendor_key}/{connection_id}`.

See `docs/integration-setup-example.md` for a full worked example (catalog read through
create/validate/save/connect/poll/kind-selection) with real request/response JSON.

get.summary: Get connection detail, including masked auth configs and kind configs.
get.description:
Fetches one connection's full detail: the raw connection sub-doc, its auth field
configs (secret-masked per `get_vendor_connection_auth_configs`'s own masking rules --
support users without `relyanceSecretAccess`, or the `hide-integration-secrets` tenant
flag), and its kind field configs.

Every auth custom field carries `isTopLevel`: for an `IN_HOST_BYOK` connection only these fields
stay in the Relyance form; every other credential field lives in the customer's secret. The
connection sub-doc carries `auth.secret_ref` (the ARN of the customer's secret -- a location,
not a secret) when set; `auth.secret_path` is never returned.

patch.summary: Update scalar sub-doc fields on a connection.
patch.description:
Updates one or more scalar sub-doc fields on an existing connection
(`refreshFrequency`, `startScanFrom`, `dataStorageLocation`, `businessNodeIds`,
`credentialsExpireAt`, `connectionName`, `relyanceSecretAccess`, `runtimeMode`). Only fields
present in the request body are written, via dotted-path `$set`/`$unset` in one update --
never a whole-document replace.

`runtimeMode` (mirrors mgr's `updateIntegrationConnectionRuntimeMode`): the tenant must have a
deployment for the mode, as mgr's `getSupportedIntegrationConnectionRuntimeModes` decides --
`IN_HOST`/`IN_HOST_BYOK` need an enabled InHost (`sierra_configuration`), `IN_HOME` an enabled
InHome (`molokai_configuration`); otherwise 422 and nothing is written. Switching to
`IN_HOST_BYOK` drops `auth.secret_path` in the same write and then deletes that Relyance-held
Secret Manager secret (3 attempts): BYOK credentials live only in the customer's environment. If
the deletion still fails, the mode change stays committed (204), the secret's path is recorded in
`auth.pending_secret_deletion`, and the next runtime-mode change retries it (and clears the field).
Switching to any other mode clears `auth.secret_ref`, which only means something for
`IN_HOST_BYOK`.

When the write includes `refreshFrequency` and/or `startScanFrom`, a best-effort "conductor
poke" is scheduled off the request path afterward (mirrors mgr's
`connSetRefreshFrequency`/`connSetStartScanFrom`) so the scan scheduler picks up the new
cadence without waiting for a restart. The poke never blocks or fails the response --
scheduling or publishing it is not on the request's critical path.

Returns 204 with no body, including when the request body has no recognized fields to write
(a no-op). Poll `GET .../{connection_id}` to observe the updated resource.

delete.summary: Delete a connection (best-effort secret cleanup first).
delete.description:
Deletes a connection. Best-effort deletes its GCP Secret Manager secret first (mirrors
`deleteConnectionSecrets` -- a no-op, not an error, if the connection never had a secret),
then `$unset`s the `vendors.integrations.<id>` sub-doc.

Returns 204 with no body.

post.summary: Validate auth-field values without persisting them.
post.description:
Validates a set of auth-field values against the vendor's auth form without persisting
anything (`Field.fill()` + `validate()`).

When the connection's `runtime_mode` is `IN_HOST_BYOK`, every credential field of the auth
method lives in the customer's own secret, so only `is_top_level` fields (e.g.
`data_storage_location`) are validated. The result is invalid when a secret field carries a
value (the error names the keys, never the values), when `secretRef` breaks a secret-reference
rule (see `PUT .../auth`), or when an app-token (browser sign-in) auth method is combined with a
secret reference. 500 when the InHost deployment cannot be read to check the reference. Relyance does not test access to the customer's secret. On any other runtime mode a
non-empty `secretRef` is invalid.

put.summary: Save auth-field values (is_top_level split; secrets to GCP Secret Manager).
put.description:
Saves auth-field values for a connection. Fields flagged `is_top_level` on the vendor's
auth form are written as flat scalars on the connection sub-doc; every other field is
stored as a GCP Secret Manager secret.

`IN_HOST_BYOK` connections never have server-side secrets: every credential field of the auth
method (secret and non-secret) lives in the customer's environment -- a Kubernetes secret, or
the AWS Secrets Manager secret named by `secretRef`. Only `is_top_level` values, `auth.type`
and `auth.secret_ref` are stored; other non-secret values are ignored. `secretRef`: omitted or
null keeps the stored value, an empty string clears it, anything else must be an AWS Secrets
Manager ARN (`arn:<partition>:secretsmanager:<region>:<account-id>:secret:<name>`, region inside
the partition) whose (partition, account) is the tenant's InHost (Outpost) deployment on AWS. It
is rejected when the tenant has no enabled InHost deployment or it is on GCP ("Secret references
are available only for Outpost on AWS."), and when the deployment's AWS account is unknown; a
failure to read the deployment is 500 (fail closed). 422 (nothing written) when a secret field
carries a value (the error names the keys, never the values), when `secretRef` is invalid, when
an app-token (browser sign-in) auth method would be used with a secret reference, or when a
required `is_top_level` field has no value (submitted, or already stored on the connection). A
non-empty `secretRef` on any other runtime mode is 422.

For `IN_HOST`/`IN_HOME` runtime-mode connections, the secret is stored in (and the
`auth.secret_path` built against) the tenant's own GCP project rather than the service's
default project. Every save also sets `auth.updated_at` (epoch seconds); when secret fields
were saved it additionally sets `auth.credentials_fingerprint` -- a SHA-256 digest of the
saved secret fields only, letting a future Terraform provider detect credential drift
without ever reading a secret value back.

Returns 204 with no body.

post.summary: Validate kind-parameter values without persisting them.
post.description:
Validates a set of parameter values against one of the vendor's kind forms
(`Field.fill()` + `validate()` -- kind params have no BYOK branch).

put.summary: Save parameter values for an already-selected kind.
put.description:
Saves parameter values for one of a connection's already-selected kinds
(`kinds.<kind>.customFields`). The kind must already exist on the connection.

Returns 204 with no body.

put.summary: Select or deselect an IntegrationKind on a connection.
put.description:
Selects or deselects an `IntegrationKind` on a connection (mirrors mgr's `connSetCheckbox`
mutation, which takes the same single `selected: bool` argument). Selecting a kind for the
first time creates its `kinds.<kind>` sub-doc (`{isSelected, customFields: []}`); selecting
one that already exists only flips its `isSelected` flag, leaving any saved `customFields`
in place. `INTEGRATION_KIND_ASSETS_DISCOVERY` and `INTEGRATION_KIND_AI_DISCOVERY` are always
forced to selected regardless of the request body -- they're always enabled and hidden from
the UI. Once a kind has a `kinds.<kind>`
entry (selected or not), `PUT .../kinds/{kind}` can save parameters for it.

Returns 204 with no body.

post.summary: Kick off a live connect/test attempt (async; poll GET for the result).
post.description:
Kicks off a live connect/test attempt for a connection and returns 202 immediately with a
monitor body `{"id", "status": "connecting"}`; the actual vendor-API call (dispatched by
AuthType) runs in the background and updates `auth.status`/`auth.error` on completion. Poll
`GET .../connections/{connection_id}` to observe the result.

`IN_HOST_BYOK` connections are not tested live (Relyance does not hold their credentials; the
scanner reports credential problems on its next scan): the connection is marked
`AUTH_STATUS_CONNECTED` before the 202 returns. 422 when the auth method is app token (browser
sign-in) and the connection has a `secret_ref`.

Marks a connection as disconnected (`auth.status = AUTH_STATUS_NOT_CONNECTED`). Purely a
Mongo write -- no vendor-API call.

Returns 204 with no body.
